Build a Sepsis-3 cohort ID list for a source, optionally importing it

Source: R/pipeline.R
build_sepsis_cohort.Rd

Source-aware Sepsis-3 cohort selection: resolves the right packaged inst/sql/{family}/cohorts/sepsis3/ SQL chain via src_family(src_name), runs it over the raw CSVs through the DuckDB-backed cohort_sql/ setup_sql selection route (suspicion of infection + absolute SOFA >= 2 within the suspicion window [-48h, +24h] - see each chain's own README for the full clinical definition and per-family adaptations), and returns the matching cohort IDs. When import = TRUE (the default), also feeds the result straight into import_cohort_general(direct_ids_path = ...) for you - no separate manual CSV round-trip needed.

Usage

build_sepsis_cohort(
  src_name,
  base_dir = NULL,
  raw_data_root = NULL,
  out_csv = NULL,
  import = TRUE,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  bundle = "sepsis3",
  import_scope = "hospital",
  memory_limit = NULL,
  threads = NULL,
  show_progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

src_name

Source name (e.g. "mimic_iii_demo").

base_dir

Project root with the source's raw demo data.

raw_data_root

Optional parent storage-root override for raw source data. The source directory is derived as {raw_data_root}/{src_name}. Forwarded to both the cohort-selection step (.ehr_select_cohort_ids_duckdb()) and the import step (import_cohort_general()), so both agree on where the raw CSVs live.

out_csv

Optional path to write the full cohort_sql result (every ID column selected, not just key) to CSV. If NULL and import = TRUE, a temporary file is used internally and removed afterward.

import

If TRUE (default), import the selected cohort via import_cohort_general(direct_ids_path = ...).

overwrite

Passed to import_cohort_general() when import = TRUE. Default FALSE.

bundle

Which cohort definition to run against the packaged Sepsis-3 SQL chain (the setup_sql chain itself is unchanged either way). Default "sepsis3": every ICU stay that met Sepsis-3 criteria, with the qualifying suspicion-of-infection event anywhere in the stay - this answers "was this patient ever septic during their ICU course", which runs much higher than admission-time sepsis-prevalence studies (e.g. on mimic_iii_demo, 95 ICU stays of 70 patients are captured). "first_sepsis3": further restricted to only a patient's absolute first-ever ICU stay (septic or not) - the sepsis3-mimic (Johnson et al. 2018) study-cohort restriction (mimic_iii_demo: 95 -> 66 stays). For eICU, cross-hospitalization ordering for "first_sepsis3" is only approximate (eICU has no exact cross-admission timestamp, only a year-granularity discharge year), so ties within the same discharge year are broken by patienthealthsystemstayid: reproducible, though not necessarily chronological. "sepsis3_admission": instead restricted to stays whose qualifying suspicion-of-infection event falls within +/-1 day of ICU/unit admission - the sepsis3-mimic suspicion-timing exclusion; a smaller effect on its own (mimic_iii_demo: 95 -> 88). "first_sepsis3_admission": both restrictions together (mimic_iii_demo: 61) - the closest packaged match to the sepsis3-mimic study population, but still well above that study's own suspected-infection count (sepsis_suspicion: 28, pre-SOFA) because it doesn't reproduce that study's separate adult/MetaVision/CSURG exclusions - those are specific to that one MIMIC-III-era study, not part of the Sepsis-3 clinical definition shared with MIMIC-IV/eICU, and live in sepsis_suspicion/sepsis_suspicion_modified instead.

import_scope

Passed to import_cohort_general() when import = TRUE. Default "hospital": for every Sepsis-3-positive ICU stay, also pulls in any other ICU stay within the SAME hospitalization, but not a patient's other, separate hospitalizations. Sepsis-3 is common enough in a general ICU population (58% of all mimic_iii patients qualify at least once) that the engine's own default of NULL (full patient history, every hospitalization a patient ever had) ends up including ~83% of the entire chartevents table - almost the whole dataset, not a focused cohort. Pass import_scope = NULL to restore that full patient-history behavior, or import_scope = "icu" to narrow further to just the exact Sepsis-3-positive stays themselves, with no sibling admissions or stays at all. Changing this always requires a full rebuild (overwrite = TRUE) - there's no cheap way to re-scope an already-built cohort.

memory_limit, threads

Optional DuckDB resource settings forwarded to the cohort-selection step (.ehr_select_cohort_ids_duckdb()) - the setup_sql chain scans full raw tables (e.g. a full CHARTEVENTS), which can exceed DuckDB's default memory cap on a memory-constrained machine. Unlike import_cohort_general()'s cohort-table build, this chain runs as plain GROUP BY/window SQL (SOFA, vitalsign, ...) and cannot be split into row-hash chunks the way a straight table copy can.

show_progress

Print each setup_sql file before execution, followed by elapsed seconds on completion or failure. Also forwarded to import_cohort_general() for the import half.

Value

Invisibly returns a one-column data frame of unique key values (the Sepsis-3 cohort IDs).

Details

Works for any source family with a packaged chain (mimic_iii, mimic_iv, eicu).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ids <- build_sepsis_cohort("mimic_iii_demo", base_dir = "/path/to/project")
# Selection only, no import:
ids <- build_sepsis_cohort("eicu_demo", base_dir = "/path/to/project",
                           import = FALSE)
# Full patient history instead of just the septic hospitalization:
ids <- build_sepsis_cohort("mimic_iii_demo", base_dir = "/path/to/project",
                           import_scope = NULL, overwrite = TRUE)
# Only each patient's first-ever ICU stay (Johnson et al. 2018 restriction):
ids <- build_sepsis_cohort("mimic_iii_demo", base_dir = "/path/to/project",
                           bundle = "first_sepsis3")
} # }
